wire.runtime_memory.approval_stop_local_.role: approval prompt for a forced stop
wire.runtime_memory.approval_stop_local_.note: {address} is the session address (keep verbatim). Must say it signals even while working and that work in flight is cut; the plain stop's prompt promises the opposite.

wire.runtime_memory.enabled.help.note: 'dormant' matches the sessions tool's stop vocabulary (wakes/monitors kept, not firing until reopened). 'TUI window' is the terminal app the operator is using; it is never ended by this guard.

wire.runtime_memory.enabled.label.note: Row label for the on/off switch; same words as the 'on' choice description, as an imperative.

wire.runtime_memory.limit_mb.help.note: Keep 1024 and 0 as digits; MiB as in the label. A value below 1024 is ignored (the default applies), not raised.

wire.runtime_memory.limit_mb.label.note: MiB (mebibytes), the unit the guard measures and reports in; use the locale's usual MiB symbol.

wire.runtime_memory.section.title.note: The per-session-runtime memory ceiling; distinct from 'Command memory limit' (per bash command).

wire.runtime_memory.stop_force_hint.role: tool-result line appended under a stop refusal
wire.runtime_memory.stop_force_hint.note: Model-and-operator-facing. Keep stop and force=true verbatim (a tool argument), and SIGTERM/SIGKILL verbatim. Safety facts that must survive: the escalation is only for an operator request or a memory runaway, and it cuts the work in flight.
